<description>
Implements a way to track the memory footprint of all non-mempool transactions that are still being referenced by block templates, see discussion in  #33899. It does not impose a limit.

IPC clients can query this footprint (total, across all clients) using the `getMemoryLoad()` IPC method. Its client-side usage is demonstrated here:
- https://github.com/stratum-mining/sv2-tp/pull/63

Additionally, the functional test in `interface_ipc.py` is expanded to demonstrate how template memory management works: templates are not released until the client drops references to them, or calls the template destroy method, or disconnects. The destroy method is called automatically by clients using [libmultiprocess](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess), as [sv2-tp](https://github.com/stratum-mining/sv2-tp) does. In the Python tests it also happens when references are destroyed or go out of scope.

Commits:

- _refactor: move CTransactionRefComp to util/hasher_
- _mining: track non-mempool memory usage_: add `TxTemplateMap` to `BlockTemplateManager` to track how many templates contain any given transaction. This map is updated by the `BlockTemplate` constructor and destructor.
- _mining: add GetTemplateMemoryUsage()_ - loops over this map and sums up the memory footprint for transactions outside the mempool (includes a fuzzer)
- _ipc: add getMemoryLoad()_ expose this information to IPC clients and add test coverage
</description>

[2026-11-10] rc:4526556635 inline on src/node/block_template_manager.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-10):
In commit "mining: add GetTemplateMemoryUsage()" (8e62f61108ca9bca0a374803dd4b8deab5fcc2c5)

I think this should throw instead of skipping the transaction. A null transaction in a template would be a bug we want to know about, and it would make the result unreliable, so it's not worth returning a number. `CHECK_NONFATAL(tx_ref);` would do this, and its documentation recommends it over `Assume` for interfaces like this one. Over IPC the exception is logged and returned to the client as an error, so the node keeps running.

`exists()` checks whether the mempool has a transaction with the same wtxid, not whether it holds this object. If a transaction is evicted and later relayed back, the mempool entry is a different `CTransaction` object, and the template's copy is kept alive only by the template but is no longer counted. Comparing pointers would count it, at the same cost:

```cpp
if (m_mempool.get(tx_ref->GetWitnessHash()) == tx_ref) continue;
```

Not important since the result is an estimate, so feel free to ignore.

re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33922#discussion_r4526609111

In commit "mining: track block templates held by IPC clients" (dd94e47ae7a035abee82901d1c33908abc9abcc3)

I think this destructor can run after `node.block_template_manager` is reset at shutdown, which would hit the `Assert` (or, if it races with the reset, use a destroyed mutex). `Shutdown()` [disconnects IPC clients](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/a5bcd06c8da4729eeaf33a84525e3c67f1cc3635/src/init.cpp#L409-L412) and [later resets the manager](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/a5bcd06c8da4729eeaf33a84525e3c67f1cc3635/src/init.cpp#L426), but when a connection is dropped, libmultiprocess destroys the server objects [asynchronously](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/a5bcd06c8da4729eeaf33a84525e3c67f1cc3635/src/ipc/libmultiprocess/include/mp/proxy-io.h#L625-L649) on a separate thread, so templates a client was still holding are not necessarily gone by the time the manager is reset.

A simple fix could be to make `NodeContext::block_template_manager` a `shared_ptr` and give `BlockTemplateImpl` a `weak_ptr` to it, so the destructor only unregisters if the manager still exists:

```cpp
~BlockTemplateImpl() override
{
    if (auto manager{m_manager.lock()}) manager->UnregisterTemplate(m_block_template);
}
```

If the destructor runs at the same time as the reset, the manager is just destroyed slightly later, after `UnregisterTemplate()` returns. That is safe because `UnregisterTemplate()` and the manager's destructor only use its own members, not the mempool or chainstate it refers to. A side benefit is that templates unregister from the manager they registered with, so the test case described in the `UnregisterTemplate()` comment, where a template unregisters from a newer manager, would go away.
